purpose: Click is a BSD-3-Clause Python library for building composable command-line interfaces. It provides decorators and classes (Command, Group, Option, Argument) that parse argv, convert values through typed ParamType objects, dispatch to nested subcommands, render help, provide shell tab-completion, and offer terminal utilities (prompts, styled echo, progress bars, pagers) and a CliRunner for testing. The repo declares version 8.5.1 (pyproject.toml L3) and CHANGES.md L1-3 dates that release 2026-11-09.
intended_users: Python developers writing command-line tools and scripts who want a decorator-based, composable CLI framework. Its tests and docs also serve maintainers and contributors (CONTRIBUTING via README L56-62, and the docs and typing tox envs in pyproject.toml).

entry_points.description: Public package API. Re-exports Command, Group, Option, Argument, Context, decorators (command, group, option, argument, pass_context, ...), exceptions, types (INT, Choice, Path, File, ...) and termui helpers (echo, prompt, confirm, progressbar, style, ...). Lazily warns on deprecated names via module __getattr__ (L76-144).

Command.main(): the standard script entry point. Reads sys.argv (with Windows glob expansion), handles shell completion, builds the Context, invokes the command, and maps exceptions to exit codes (Command.main L1483-1617).
Command._main_shell_completion(): checks the _<PROG>_COMPLETE environment variable and delegates to shell_completion.shell_complete, then exits (L1619-1649).
@click.command decorator: wraps a function into a Command, attaching options and arguments declared with @option and @argument (decorators.py L168-262; @argument L324, @option L352).
@click.group decorator: same as command but creates a Group (multi-command container) (decorators.py L293-313).
CliRunner: in-process invocation for tests, with output and stdin capture (CliRunner L317-351, invoke L595).

key_modules.role: Core object model. Context (L213) holds per-invocation state and invoke/fail/exit. Command (L960) has make_context, parse_args, invoke, and main. Group (L1671) adds subcommand resolution, chaining, and invoke_without_command. Parameter (L2209) with Option (L2891) and Argument (L3698) handles value sourcing (consume_value L2518), type conversion (type_cast_value L2566), defaults and envvars (process_value L2640), and parse-result handling (handle_parse_result L2763). ParameterSource enum (L174).

Internal option parser modelled on optparse (_OptionParser L224). Tokenizes argv into option values, positional arguments, and an ordering list. It is wrapped by Command.make_parser and Command.parse_args. Deprecated as a public API (L237-238).

Parameter type system. ParamType base (L65) with convert/fail. Concrete types: StringParamType (L304), Choice (L342), DateTime (L522), IntParamType/IntRange (L736/744), FloatParamType/FloatRange (L768/776), BoolParamType (L819), UUIDParameterType (L888), File (L915), Path (L1059), Tuple (L1258). convert_type (L1356) maps Python defaults to types.

Decorator-based API that builds Command, Group, Option, and Argument, plus helpers such as pass_context, pass_obj, make_pass_decorator, version_option, help_option, confirmation_option, and password_option.

Shell tab-completion. shell_complete (L19) dispatches on the env var instruction (source or complete). ShellComplete base class (L277) with Bash (L388), Zsh (L447), Fish (L479), and PowerShell (L516) subclasses. CompletionItem (L67). add_completion_class and get_completion_class (L560/588) form a registry.
Help-text layout. HelpFormatter (L110) writes usage, sections, and definition lists with indentation and width, plus wrap_text (L31) and measure_table (L14).

Exception hierarchy used for user-facing errors and exit codes. ClickException (L35) is the base, with UsageError (L68), BadParameter (L114), MissingParameter (L159), NoSuchOption (L232), NoSuchCommand (L268), FileError (L342). Abort (L362) and Exit (L366) are control-flow signals.

Interactive terminal utilities: prompt (L139/168), confirm (L289), progressbar (L403-443), style and secho (L641/780), edit (L815), launch (L923), getchar (L957), pause (L993), echo_via_pager (L367). Platform implementations live in _termui_impl.py and _winconsole.py.

Misc helpers: echo (L240), open_file (L381), format_filename (L430), get_app_dir (L472), _LazyFile (L103), _detect_program_name (L550), _expand_args (L605, Windows glob expansion used by Command.main).
Thread-local current-context stack. get_current_context (L20), push_context (L44), pop_context (L49), resolve_color_default (L54).
Test harness. CliRunner (L317) isolates stdin/stdout/env and invokes a command in-process. Result (L231) wraps output, exit_code, and exception. Capture modes are 'sys' or 'fd' (docstring L331-338).

Private, platform-specific and compatibility helpers. _winconsole handles Windows console I/O; _termui_impl holds ProgressBar (L44) and pager/edit internals; _compat handles stream and atomic-file details.
public_interfaces: private (underscore-prefixed); not part of the public API

execution_flow: 1) A script's console entry calls cli() which is Command.__call__ -> Command.main (core.py L1483, L1651). 2) main resolves args (sys.argv[1:], Windows-expanded at L1534-1540) and prog_name (L1542-1543). 3) _main_shell_completion (L1546, L1619-1649) checks _PROG_COMPLETE; if set it calls shell_completion.shell_complete and exits. 4) main calls self.make_context(prog_name, args) (L1559). make_context (L1330-1365) builds a Context (context_class) and calls parse_args inside ctx.scope(). 5) Command.parse_args (L1367-1398) creates a parser via make_parser (L1227), gets opts, leftover args, and order from _OptionParser.parse_args (parser.py L298-314), then calls param.handle_parse_result for each parameter in processing order (iter_params_for_processing, core.py L147). 6) handle_parse_result (L2763) calls consume_value (L2518: CLI value, then envvar, then default_map, then default) and process_value (L2640), which runs type_cast_value (L2566) and the ParamType.convert (types.py L65). Leftover args are stored in ctx.args. 7) main calls self.invoke(ctx) (L1560). For a plain Command, invoke (L1400-1414) calls ctx.invoke(callback, **ctx.params). For a Group (core.py L2020-2086), it resolves the subcommand with resolve_command (L2088-2112), which uses get_command/list_commands, then creates the sub-context with cmd.make_context(parent=ctx) and invokes it. In chain mode it creates all subcontexts first and invokes them in order. 8) Exceptions are caught in main (L1571-1617): Exit gives an exit code, Abort and KeyboardInterrupt print 'Aborted', ClickException shows its message and exit code (exceptions.py L35). The process then ends with sys.exit (L1612). With standalone_mode=False, main returns the value or re-raises instead. For tests, CliRunner.invoke (testing.py L595) runs main with standalone_mode and captures output into Result."}]
